# `Q-10-5` — Unresolved Partial Reference

> A `$partial(name)$` reference was not resolved during
> template compilation.

## What this means

The template engine resolves partial references at compile
time: each `$partial("name")$` is replaced with the parsed body
of the named partial. This error fires when an unresolved
reference survives into the evaluation stage — the engine
should have substituted it but did not.

In day-to-day use this presents as a missing-partial error
from a different code path than `Q-10-3`. If you are seeing it
and not also `Q-10-3`, the situation is likely a Quarto bug
rather than a source-level mistake.

## Why this happens

The unresolved reference reaches evaluation either because the
compile-time resolution step was skipped (a programmatic
caller bypassing the normal compile path) or because the
resolution step silently dropped a reference it should have
flagged.

## How to fix

Confirm the partial exists, as you would for `Q-10-3`. If the
partial is present and `Q-10-3` is not also reported, report
the template and the calling configuration at the Quarto issue
tracker — the failure path is unusual.

## Related

- `Q-10-3` — partial not found: the same underlying problem
  surfaced earlier in the pipeline.
- `Q-10-4` — recursive partial: a related partial-resolution
  failure.
